title_en: Common reasons your Roku TV can turn on by itself and how to fix it
title_fa: Common reasons your Roku TV can turn on by itself and how to fix it
excerpt_en: If your TV has randomly been turning on and it has a Roku attached to it, it could be your Roku's doing. Check these settings.
excerpt_fa: If your TV has randomly been turning on and it has a Roku attached to it, it could be your Roku's doing. Check these settings.
content_en:
Common reasons your Roku TV can turn on by itself and how to fix it
Some people have been experiencing random power-ons recently.
You're sound asleep in the middle of the night when, all of a sudden, your TV turns on. You know you turned off the TV before you went to bed, no one else is awake, and there's nothing near your remote to accidentally push the power button. What — or who — could have turned on the TV? A bored spirit haunting your home? A burglar looking to take a quick break?
Those scenarios are highly unlikely. But, unfortunately, some Roku TVs and Roku streaming device owners have been jolted out of their slumber by those products inexplicably powering on randomly over the past few months. And no one really knows why it's happening. There may be a few explanations, however, and a couple of potential fixes to try if your Roku device has gone rogue during the wee hours.
A bug in Roku OS 15.3
When Roku OS version 15.3 went live in August 2026, owners of Roku TVs and Roku streaming devices began reporting these middle-of-the-night disturbances. Not every Roku TV or streaming player has been impacted by this supposed 15.3 bug, but the timing of the reports with the software update seems more than coincidental.
What's odd about that, though, is that there was nothing in the 15.3 update that involved autoplay features or even power management. So, in theory, the changes that were made to the Roku OS shouldn't have spurred these instances of people's Roku TVs "waking up" without being powered on by anyone (or anything) and playing a TV show or movie. But we all know that software updates often introduce bugs with no real rhyme or reason, and that feels like the most logical explanation for these strange occurrences.
A glitchy HDMI-CEC connection
Having your Roku TV's HDMI-CEC feature enabled is another very plausible reason the TV powers on randomly. If you're not familiar with HDMI-CEC, it's basically a chain that links all your A/V components with built-in HDMI switching (like soundbars, gaming consoles, receivers and speakers) since they're all connected via HDMI cables. And this allows all of those devices to be controlled with one remote.
So, when you power on your Roku TV, for example, HDMI-CEC essentially notifies all the other connected components to turn on. All it takes is one glitchy signal to confuse the whole chain, which could lead to a random power-up. And there is a history of HDMI-CEC causing strange switching between inputs and components, as well as phantom power-ons. Samsung Anynet+, Sony BRAVIA Sync, LG SimpLink and Roku 1-Touch Play are all just different names for the same HDMI-CEC standard, but each has its own custom software added to it to create the proprietary HDMI-CEC feature for each brand of smart TV.
Unfortunately, compatibility sometimes becomes an issue unless all of your connected devices are made by the same company (though even that doesn't guarantee incident-free performance). This can cause signal miscommunication that results in the random behavior of your Roku TV or streaming device.
Fast TV Start
There are other possible explanations for your Roku TV turning on by itself. For example, the Fast TV Start feature is a proprietary power-management setting that keeps your Roku TV's OS on in the background even when you shut off the TV.
This allows the TV to turn on instantly without any boot time, and it keeps the TV on alert for voice commands to turn the TV back on. Fast TV Start has also seemingly caused phantom power-on problems in conjunction with the Roku OS 15.3 update, as the always-on network connection kept open the door for overnight glitches.
How to prevent your Roku TV from turning on by itself
You may try all of these suggestions and still not have much luck because the root of the issue has not been "officially" identified by Roku, or anyone else, for that matter. And without the root cause, there remains no guaranteed fix. But these possible solutions are certainly worth trying and just might do the trick.
The first thing to try, if you haven't already, is updating your Roku TV's OS to version 16, which was released in October. Fixing the 15.3 bug wasn't part of the update, and no reports have surfaced that OS 16 patched the automatic power-on problem, but it's definitely worth trying. The worst-case scenario is that your Roku TV's OS is fully updated.
Next, disable 1-Touch Play (HDMI-CEC) not just on your Roku TV but on all the other components connected to the TV, regardless of brand. This includes your A/V equipment and gaming consoles. To do so on your Roku TV, go to Settings > System > Control other devices and uncheck 1-Touch Play. Also disable Fast TV Start, which you can find under Settings > System > Power > Fast TV Start, then either clear the Enable Fast TV Start option or check Off to disable it.
If these don't work, try unplugging the TV when you're done watching it each night (no, not ideal), using a smart plug to automatically cut the power for you or consulting Roku's tech support portal at support.roku.com for further assistance.

Next, disable 1-Touch Play (HDMI-CEC) not just on your Roku TV but on all the other components connected to the TV, regardless of brand. This includes your A/V equipment and gaming consoles. To do so on your Roku TV, go to Settings > System > Control other devices and uncheck 1-Touch Play. Also disable Fast TV Start, which you can find under Settings > System > Power > Fast TV Start, then either clear the Enable Fast TV Start option or check Off to disable it.
If these don't work, try unplugging the TV when you're done watching it each night (no, not ideal), using a smart plug to automatically cut the power for you or consulting Roku's tech support portal at support.roku.com for further assistance.

title_en: One cable mistake could be killing your desktop PC's gaming performance
title_fa: One cable mistake could be killing your desktop PC's gaming performance
excerpt_en: Plugging your monitor into the motherboard instead of your dedicated GPU can ruin gaming performance. Here's how to check your ports and get your frames back.
excerpt_fa: Plugging your monitor into the motherboard instead of your dedicated GPU can ruin gaming performance. Here's how to check your ports and get your frames back.
content_en:
One cable mistake could be killing your desktop PC's gaming performance
Your monitor might be connected to the motherboard instead of your graphics card, and the fix takes only a cable swap.
You may have a great graphics card in your gaming desktop and still be disappointed with its performance because of where the monitor is plugged in. Many PCs have HDMI, DisplayPort and USB-C monitor connections in two places: on the motherboard and on the dedicated graphics card. The same cable can fit either set of ports, which isn't particularly helpful.
If your desktop has a dedicated graphics card, the monitor should normally connect to that card's outputs. You may end up with less capable integrated graphics or a blank screen if you use a motherboard port. Instead of assuming that the problem is your hardware, start by inspecting the back of the case. The motherboard's video outputs typically use the graphics integrated into the CPU (if it has any), instead of the dedicated graphics card in a PCIe slot.
Why plugging into the motherboard can hurt gaming performance
Integrated graphics are suitable for basic tasks and less demanding games, but typically cannot compete with your dedicated graphics card — even if you know how to boost GPU performance without buying new hardware. If Windows runs your game on integrated graphics instead, you're missing out on the performance of your dedicated GPU.
Plugging into the motherboard doesn't always leave the dedicated GPU idle. In some Windows configurations, that card can still render games and pass the frames through integrated graphics, potentially adding overhead. Microsoft doesn't state a percentage of performance loss for this configuration, and the impact will depend on the hardware. That's why some gamers don't notice the mistake immediately.
For others, it's a black screen. Motherboard video outputs won't work with Intel desktop processors carrying an F or KF suffix, since those chips lack integrated graphics. Some PCs also disable the integrated GPU when a dedicated card is installed, so a blank screen doesn't necessarily mean your graphics card has failed.
How to make sure you're using the right port
Luckily, the correct ports are typically easy to find. The motherboard's video outputs are grouped with its USB, Ethernet and audio ports. The graphics card has its own outputs on a separate expansion bracket, typically lower down on the back of a conventional tower. They're often horizontal rather than vertical, but orientation isn't universal, so check which ports belong to the graphics card.
Turn off the PC, move the monitor cable to the graphics card and select the corresponding input on the monitor. Both HDMI and DisplayPort support high-refresh-rate gaming, provided your graphics card, monitor and cable support the resolution and refresh rate you want. DisplayPort comes standard on most modern gaming monitors, but if you are already using HDMI and it is working at the resolution and refresh rate you need, then you don't need to purchase a new cable. For Windows 11, go to Settings > System > Display > Advanced display and check the refresh rate.
Do remember, though, that a 100Hz monitor that's set to 60Hz will only show 60 updates per second, no matter what the graphics card renders. If your screen goes black after switching to the graphics card, try a different GPU port or cable. Before checking the power connectors or seating on the card, shut down and unplug the PC. Finally, if integrated graphics aren't disabled, you can even connect a second monitor to the motherboard's output, depending on your system's compatibility.

title_en: Why your SD card won't let you transfer files bigger than 4GB, and how to fix it
title_fa: Why your SD card won't let you transfer files bigger than 4GB, and how to fix it
excerpt_en: Some SD cards just won't accept files larger than 4GB, no matter the total capacity or how much free storage there is. But don't worry, it's not hard to fix.
excerpt_fa: Some SD cards just won't accept files larger than 4GB, no matter the total capacity or how much free storage there is. But don't worry, it's not hard to fix.
content_en:
Why your SD card won't let you transfer files bigger than 4GB, and how to fix it
Your SD card's file system might be stopping you from transferring large files, but there's an easy fix for that.
SD card capacities have grown by leaps and bounds since hitting the market in the early 2000s, and the best microSD cards now come in capacities from 128GB up to a massive 1TB. No matter how capacious your SD card, though, you may run into an unexpected limitation: it won't accept files larger than 4GB, even when there's enough space left.
While it may seem worrying, the good news is that the SD card itself is almost certainly fine. Instead, the problem lies in the file format it's currently using. More specifically, it's FAT32, a file system that dates back to Windows 95 and is still commonly used today. Although it's widely compatible and can be read by almost any device, it has a major downside: no single file can be larger than 4GB.
FAT32's 4GB-per-file limit comes down to how it records file sizes using a 32-bit number. In computing, the largest value that fits within this limit is 4,294,967,295 bytes, or nearly 4GB. The SD card can physically hold files over 4GB, but the file system prevents it. That's usually fine if you only store documents and photos, but it can quickly become a problem if you want to store 4K videos, for example. In that case, you'll need to reformat your microSD card to exFAT, another file system designed to overcome FAT32's limitations — including support for files larger than 4GB.
How to format your SD card on Windows and macOS
First, back up all the files on your SD card, since this process will erase everything. Also, if you're using very old tech (like a camera that's more than a decade old), it may not support exFAT. Microsoft added exFAT support in Windows Vista SP1, while Apple added it with OS X Snow Leopard. If your device predates either OS, it's probably best to keep your SD card formatted as FAT32.
On Windows, open File Explorer to format your SD card. Click This PC, then right-click on your SD card. Select Format from the menu that appears and choose exFAT under File System. Here, you can also choose whether to run a Quick Format or rename the volume. The process is the same as formatting a microSD card or a USB drive. On a Mac, use the Disk Utility app instead (you can quickly find it using Spotlight). With the app open, go to the View menu and click Show All Devices. Select your SD card — not the volume listed under it — then click Erase. Set the format to exFAT, name the volume and confirm.
After formatting the SD card, you can freely copy files larger than 4GB to it. If you want to switch back to FAT32, repeat the steps above and change the file system again. Keep in mind that Windows won't let you select FAT32 for cards larger than 32GB, and you'll need to use Terminal or third-party software for that.

title_en: This underrated Google Health app feature can make food tracking less annoying
title_fa: This underrated Google Health app feature can make food tracking less annoying
excerpt_en: There's a suite of features with Google's Health app, but you've likely overlooked the intuitive food tracking function that helps keep your diet in check.
excerpt_fa: There's a suite of features with Google's Health app, but you've likely overlooked the intuitive food tracking function that helps keep your diet in check.
content_en:
This underrated Google Health app feature can make food tracking less annoying
Get a handle on how your diet is affecting your overall health.
For those keeping a close eye on their health goals, the Google Health app pairs seamlessly with Fitbit trackers and Google Pixel smartwatches. The Google Health Premium subscription tier offers many upgrades to really hone in on daily intake and activity goals, such as food and hydration tracking.
It's not necessarily a unique feature. Many fitness tracker companion apps offer nutrition logging, including Oura and Garmin. There are also popular third-party apps like MyFitnessPal that have food logging capabilities. But Google Health Premium's version is incredibly intuitive, versatile and will actually make you more inclined to use it.
We live in a day and age where everything is all about protein. Are you getting enough protein? Does this yogurt, bread or bar have sufficient protein to help you meet your daily goals? Not only that, but we're also counting carbs, calories and fat, and trying to calculate whether we're eating in a deficit and meeting or exceeding goals. This sorely underrated feature of the Google Health app is one of the best upgrades with Google Health Premium that you probably aren't using yet.
Logging meals is incredibly simple
Once you sign up for Google Health Premium, available at $9.99 per month or at no extra charge through a Google One subscription, it unlocks a Nutrition section under the Health tab of the app. Here, you can see data like your calorie target (based on gender, age, height, weight, and average activity) and caloric burn and intake. It knows how many calories you burned based on steps, activity, and heart rate logged from a companion tracker or smartwatch. But how does it know how much you consumed? That's up to you to log.
There are several ways you can log a meal. Tap the "+" sign at the top right of the Nutrition card, tap the "+ Log" button under your daily summary on the Today tab, or select Food & Drink if it's within those customizable tabs. You can also select the Ask Coach assistant and type or speak details of the meal.
It's incredibly simple. Describe the meal (say "I had a coffee, banana, and coconut yogurt") or use a barcode scanner on each ingredient. The most convenient option? Just take a photo. Use that photo you were going to upload to social media anyway and upload it to the app. Alternatively, you can take one right from the app. It intelligently analyzes and identifies the dish, then calculates data from the ingredients. You can even snap a photo of a packaged item, like a box of cereal or protein bar, and watch it calculate the nutritional content accordingly.
If necessary, you can modify details as needed. Maybe you want to clarify that your Caesar salad has light dressing, for example, or that you only ate half a portion.
The nutritional information you get is so helpful
Logging is great, but what can you do with all this information? The more you log, the more helpful the data is. Working alongside a tracker like the Fitbit Air or Fitbit Edge, it can determine patterns. It may determine that you don't sleep well when you have caffeine or a heavy meal late at night. Perhaps you have more energy in workouts with a bigger breakfast. It can also provide recommendations on what to eat to stay within your caloric recommendations or meet your protein goals.
In the summary page for each day, you'll see an ongoing calculation of how many calories you have left to consume to either reach your target or remain in a caloric deficit in relation to how many calories you have burned. You'll also see macro goals, calculated from the meals you have logged. This includes carbs, fat, and protein. It advises where you should be for each and what percentage of that you're at.
Like any food logging app, it takes diligence to remember to add everything you consume, from your morning coffee to your afternoon snack or the cup of popcorn you snuck in at night. But it's so easy to do this by snapping photos or speaking to Ask Coach. You could sit down at night and dictate your entire day's worth of meals so it's all logged at once (and check if there's space in your calorie goals for that evening glass of wine). It's so easy to do on the fly, and one of the most underrated Google Health Premium features you should be using.

title_en: How to get better results from Google Gemini
title_fa: How to get better results from Google Gemini
excerpt_en: These tips and tricks will help you prompt Gemini better.
excerpt_fa: These tips and tricks will help you prompt Gemini better.
content_en:
How to get better results from Google Gemini
These tips and tricks will help you prompt Gemini better.
Finding the right AI search engine can be tricky. Google's most prominent AI tool is Gemini, an AI assistant designed to deliver informative, concise answers while helping with daily workflows. It's not the most feature-rich chatbot, yet its integration with Google's own apps and ecosystems makes it a strong competitor to Claude and ChatGPT. It's an powerful tool when used properly, and making it work well starts with optimizing Gemini.
Google Gemini offers a convenient way to answer basic search questions and research a range of topics, and it can be a particularly useful companion to Google's search engine and products. That starts with integrating Gemini with your apps. You can connect your most-used apps to Gemini directly under the customization menu in the Gemini menu. We highly recommend doing this to let Gemini streamline any workflows you have.
How to prompt Gemini more effectively
Prompts are the cornerstone of optimizing any AI assistant, and Google Gemini is no exception. Standard prompt advice applies here: prompts with specific, detailed instructions and added context will perform much better than generic ones. Remember that AI is malleable, including its personality and the way it delivers information. To prompt with Gemini effectively, specify its role in the conversation. Is it a close friend, a mentor or a professional in a given industry? If you struggle to come up with ideas, set restrictions. Limiting sources and presentation methods is a great way to quickly tailor Gemini to your needs.
You can also shape Gemini's responses through skills, prompts that can be saved and run with a simple slash command. You can find skills listed in the customization menu. Google offers a few premade skills by default, but you can create your own and execute them as you see fit. We recommend creating a skill for different roles you need Gemini to fulfill. Once you're done, you can simply type the command to tailor Gemini without having to swap tabs.
Tips for using Google Gemini
Gemini's responses have a few chat parameters you can use. When starting a chat with Gemini, you can click the plus icon near the chat bar to display various settings. The first few options allow you to upload documents or images, but the more impactful options are at the bottom: deep research and guided learning. Deep research tailors Gemini to act as an authority in the space, requiring it to find multiple sources on a given topic before responding. This can be a great way to get detailed responses about niche topics you'd struggle to search elsewhere. Guided learning is tailored as a study guide for those learning a new subject.
Since AI algorithms are constantly evolving, Gemini likely isn't the only chatbot you're using. Google is well aware of this and allows you to import chat history from other AI chatbots to Gemini. Export your chat data from your other chatbots, then enter the settings menu for Gemini to import that data. This will help tailor Gemini's output and give it a starting memory to draw from.

title_en: Honor Magic8 Pro vs. Magic9 Pro Max: What's been upgraded?
title_fa: Honor Magic8 Pro vs. Magic9 Pro Max: What's been upgraded?
excerpt_en: This Pro upgrade is messier than the typical year-over-year refresh, but the new flagship does give us a pretty good idea of where Honor put its priorities.
excerpt_fa: This Pro upgrade is messier than the typical year-over-year refresh, but the new flagship does give us a pretty good idea of where Honor put its priorities.
content_en:
Honor Magic8 Pro vs. Magic9 Pro Max: What's been upgraded?
A 200MP main camera and 8,800mAh battery headline Honor's new flagship, though not every spec moves forward.
If you were waiting for an Honor Magic9 Pro, you can stop. Honor hasn't announced one.
Instead, Honor's 2026 lineup tops out at the Magic9 Pro Max, with the Magic9 and Magic9 Super Edition sitting below it. It's a bit messier than the typical year-over-year Pro refresh, but the new flagship does give us a pretty good idea of where Honor allocated its upgrade budget.
The major changes are obvious: a 200MP main camera, enhanced ARRI video capabilities, a 8,800mAh battery and Qualcomm's 2nm Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Honor is a Chinese smartphone manufacturer (and yes, the Huawei tie-in does still come up), but Huawei sold the Honor business in 2020 and stated it would retain no stake or management role in the company thereafter.
The main camera, not the telephoto, is the real upgrade
While the camera bump may be shouting "more megapixels," the interesting part is where Honor put them.
The Magic8 Pro featured a 50MP 1/1.3-inch primary camera, a 200MP 1/1.4-inch telephoto camera with 3.7x optical zoom and a 50MP ultrawide camera. The Magic9 Pro Max swaps that main camera for a 200MP 1/1.28-inch sensor and retains a 200MP 1/1.4-inch telephoto camera, although Honor lists 3.5x optical zoom instead of 3.7x. Stabilization on the main and telephoto cameras also improves from Honor's CIPA 6.5 rating to CIPA 8.0.
So the dual-200MP setup is more dramatic than the generational change. The Magic8 Pro already has a 200MP telephoto. The larger upgrade is the new main sensor, which is complemented by improved stabilization and Honor's own imaging chip, the H1. And no, 200MP does not necessarily translate to higher quality photos.
Honor's real ambition lies in video. Through its ARRI partnership, the Magic9 Pro Max features LogC3 recording, ARRI Wide Gamut 3 and 10-bit capture, plus 14 preset ARRI Looks and 87 predefined color gradings. ARRI Cinema Mode tops out at 4K 60fps, giving people who color-grade footage more to work with than a cinematic filter and a dramatic name.
The phone could "introduce up-and-coming cinematographers to the ARRI brand ... [b]y giving them access to ARRI Image Science," said David Bermbach, chief product officer at ARRI. Honor leans into that creator angle with an optional Photography Master Kit containing 200mm- and 500mm-equivalent teleconverters, an imaging grip and other accessories.
That's more than putting another camera company's logo on the back. Oppo and Vivo are already pushing 200MP sensors, teleconverters and increasingly elaborate imaging systems on their own flagships, so Honor needs something besides a megapixel arms race to stand out.
The battery is much bigger, with a few catches
For comparison, the Magic8 Pro is equipped with a 7,200mAh battery, 120W wired charging and 80W wireless charging, based on the Chinese specifications (Honor varies battery specs by market). That's raised to 8,800mAh, or about 22 percent more capacity, with the Magic9 Pro Max, but wired charging is limited to 100W. Wireless charging is still 80W, and the wireless charger is sold separately.
The battery also carries some luggage. The Magic9 Pro Max is slightly heavier than the Magic8 Pro at 233 grams, and the display is slightly larger at 6.8 inches compared to 6.71 inches. It also introduces MagicOS 11, built on Android 17, with file transfers across supported iPhones, Macs, Android devices and Windows PCs. Honor Connect is required for iOS, macOS and Windows transfers.
Honor has not confirmed if the international variants will be equipped with the 8,800mAh battery. That 8,800mAh figure shouldn't be assumed for other markets, as the Magic8 Pro in the United Kingdom has a 6,270mAh battery, while China's version has a 7,200mAh battery.
The company hasn't even confirmed a US release, so anyone who's considered importing it would have to check network-band support, warranty coverage and regional software differences rather than assume it will act like a locally bought Galaxy or Pixel. The Magic9 Pro Max starts at 6,499 yuan in China (the equivalent of about $974).
content_fa:
Honor Magic8 Pro vs. Magic9 Pro Max: What's been upgraded?
A 200MP main camera and 8,800mAh battery headline Honor's new flagship, though not every spec moves forward.
If you were waiting for an Honor Magic9 Pro, you can stop. Honor hasn't announced one.
Instead, Honor's 2026 lineup tops out at the Magic9 Pro Max, with the Magic9 and Magic9 Super Edition sitting below it. It's a bit messier than the typical year-over-year Pro refresh, but the new flagship does give us a pretty good idea of where Honor allocated its upgrade budget.
The major changes are obvious: a 200MP main camera, enhanced ARRI video capabilities, a 8,800mAh battery and Qualcomm's 2nm Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Honor is a Chinese smartphone manufacturer (and yes, the Huawei tie-in does still come up), but Huawei sold the Honor business in 2020 and stated it would retain no stake or management role in the company thereafter.
The main camera, not the telephoto, is the real upgrade
While the camera bump may be shouting "more megapixels," the interesting part is where Honor put them.
The Magic8 Pro featured a 50MP 1/1.3-inch primary camera, a 200MP 1/1.4-inch telephoto camera with 3.7x optical zoom and a 50MP ultrawide camera. The Magic9 Pro Max swaps that main camera for a 200MP 1/1.28-inch sensor and retains a 200MP 1/1.4-inch telephoto camera, although Honor lists 3.5x optical zoom instead of 3.7x. Stabilization on the main and telephoto cameras also improves from Honor's CIPA 6.5 rating to CIPA 8.0.
So the dual-200MP setup is more dramatic than the generational change. The Magic8 Pro already has a 200MP telephoto. The larger upgrade is the new main sensor, which is complemented by improved stabilization and Honor's own imaging chip, the H1. And no, 200MP does not necessarily translate to higher quality photos.
Honor's real ambition lies in video. Through its ARRI partnership, the Magic9 Pro Max features LogC3 recording, ARRI Wide Gamut 3 and 10-bit capture, plus 14 preset ARRI Looks and 87 predefined color gradings. ARRI Cinema Mode tops out at 4K 60fps, giving people who color-grade footage more to work with than a cinematic filter and a dramatic name.
The phone could "introduce up-and-coming cinematographers to the ARRI brand ... [b]y giving them access to ARRI Image Science," said David Bermbach, chief product officer at ARRI. Honor leans into that creator angle with an optional Photography Master Kit containing 200mm- and 500mm-equivalent teleconverters, an imaging grip and other accessories.
That's more than putting another camera company's logo on the back. Oppo and Vivo are already pushing 200MP sensors, teleconverters and increasingly elaborate imaging systems on their own flagships, so Honor needs something besides a megapixel arms race to stand out.
The battery is much bigger, with a few catches
For comparison, the Magic8 Pro is equipped with a 7,200mAh battery, 120W wired charging and 80W wireless charging, based on the Chinese specifications (Honor varies battery specs by market). That's raised to 8,800mAh, or about 22 percent more capacity, with the Magic9 Pro Max, but wired charging is limited to 100W. Wireless charging is still 80W, and the wireless charger is sold separately.
The battery also carries some luggage. The Magic9 Pro Max is slightly heavier than the Magic8 Pro at 233 grams, and the display is slightly larger at 6.8 inches compared to 6.71 inches. It also introduces MagicOS 11, built on Android 17, with file transfers across supported iPhones, Macs, Android devices and Windows PCs. Honor Connect is required for iOS, macOS and Windows transfers.
Honor has not confirmed if the international variants will be equipped with the 8,800mAh battery. That 8,800mAh figure shouldn't be assumed for other markets, as the Magic8 Pro in the United Kingdom has a 6,270mAh battery, while China's version has a 7,200mAh battery.
The company hasn't even confirmed a US release, so anyone who's considered importing it would have to check network-band support, warranty coverage and regional software differences rather than assume it will act like a locally bought Galaxy or Pixel. The Magic9 Pro Max starts at 6,499 yuan in China (the equivalent of about $974).

title_en: Here's when a dedicated graphics card is worth it
title_fa: Here's when a dedicated graphics card is worth it
excerpt_en: Modern iGPUs are surprisingly capable, but they aren't without limitations.
excerpt_fa: Modern iGPUs are surprisingly capable, but they aren't without limitations.
content_en:
Here's when a dedicated graphics card is worth it
Modern iGPUs are surprisingly capable, but they aren’t without limitations.
A discrete graphics card is often the most expensive component in desktop computers, especially in gaming-focused builds. Besides driving a display, dedicated graphics cards also accelerate productivity-focused tasks like high resolution video editing, loading and running local LLMs or playing high-fidelity video games. While discrete graphics cards provide big performance uplifts to desktop computers, they aren't necessarily devoid of drawbacks.
If all you do on your computer is browse the web, stream media and play casual games, investing in a dedicated GPU might be unnecessary, and that doesn't even count buying a compatible PSU to power the card itself. Instead, you can look toward integrated graphics, as modern iGPUs are quite competent at offering a solid desktop experience, including light productivity, seamless media encoding and decoding and even casual gaming. As the name suggests, an integrated GPU is built into the same processor package and shares memory bandwidth with the CPU, unlike dedicated GPUs that have their own VRAM.
If you're on the fence deciding between getting a dedicated GPU or an iGPU, ask yourself if the additional power is something you actually need. If your current computing needs don't involve demanding workloads, a modern iGPU, like the AMD Radeon 780M, should easily fulfill your daily computing demands.
Not all integrated graphics are created equal
You might be surprised to learn how capable modern iGPUs have become, as they were once a bit of a drag on a system. However, it's worth noting that not all CPUs come equipped with equally capable iGPUs. Some only support display output, while others can comfortably drive high-resolution displays at higher refresh rate displays (not to confuse with pushing high frame rates in games), play casual games and handle light GPU-intensive workloads.
Take the AMD Ryzen 7 8700G and Ryzen 7 9800X3D processors, for example. The former features the AMD Radeon 780M graphics with 12 compute units, while the latter comes with basic Radeon Graphics, consisting of only two compute units. Interestingly, despite the Ryzen 7 9800X3D being significantly faster at CPU-related workloads, it's considerably weaker than the Ryzen 7 8700G in GPU-intensive scenarios.
If you're putting together a desktop computer with an iGPU, both Intel and AMD offer options across different budgets. However, AMD is currently leading the desktop iGPU space with its iGPU offerings providing substantial graphics-processing horsepower over Intel's conventional integrated graphics solutions.
When is a dedicated graphics card worth buying?
If you increasingly find your workloads shifting towards high-resolution video and photo editing or high-fidelity gaming, buying a dedicated graphics card over an iGPU makes the most sense. Not only is a discrete graphics card considerably more powerful than an iGPU, its dedicated VRAM provides a separate and much higher bandwidth memory pool that graphics workloads can take advantage of, alleviating memory-related bottlenecks that iGPUs are commonly susceptible to.
Unlike a dedicated graphics cards, an iGPU's performance depends on more than just its clock speeds or core counts. Since iGPUs share system memory, RAM speeds, configuration and capacity can all contribute to memory-related bottlenecks. For instance, TechSpot found that switching from DDR5-6400 to DDR5-5200 saw significant performance drops on the Ryzen 7 8700G, across several games.
On the bright side, owning a desktop computer means the freedom to upgrade your machine based on your needs. Just because you built a computer with an iGPU, it doesn't mean you're stuck with it forever. If you find your computing demands shifting from light workloads to running demanding games, loading heavy LLMs, rendering 3D graphics or high-resolution video editing, popping in a powerful graphics card into you PC can give it the additional horsepower needed to meet those demands. However, don't forget to verify your power supply capacity, PCIe compatibility and case clearance to accommodate a discrete graphics card into your build.

title_en: Watch SpaceX successfully execute the first ‘chopstick’ catch of Starship
title_fa: Watch SpaceX successfully execute the first ‘chopstick’ catch of Starship
excerpt_en: After aborting a planned catch of Starship Flight 15's booster, SpaceX successfully captured Starship with its "Mechazilla" launch and catch tower for the first time. The company has performed 'chopstick' catches of its boosters before, but this is the first time the maneuver...
excerpt_fa: After aborting a planned catch of Starship Flight 15's booster, SpaceX successfully captured Starship with its "Mechazilla" launch and catch tower for the first time. The company has performed 'chopstick' catches of its boosters before, but this is the first time the maneuver...
content_en:
After aborting a planned catch of Starship Flight 15’s booster, SpaceX successfully captured Starship with its “Mechazilla” launch and catch tower for the first time. The company has performed ‘chopstick’ catches of its boosters before, but this is the first time the maneuver has successfully been executed on the Starship vehicle itself.
Watch SpaceX successfully execute the first ‘chopstick’ catch of Starship
SpaceX captured Starship using the arms of ‘Mechazilla’ its launch and catch tower for the first time.
SpaceX captured Starship using the arms of ‘Mechazilla’ its launch and catch tower for the first time.
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said during the company’s third-quarter earnings call that “success is not guaranteed on these first flights, but I’d say it’s more likely than not that this succeeds next flight.” While not a complete success, in that the company was unable to recover the entire launch vehicle, it still stands as a milestone for the Starship program. And, since it has previously caught boosters on previous launches, there is reason to believe the failure today was not an insurmountable obstacle. SpaceX is still trying to determine what caused the booster to abort its landing and detonate over the Gulf of Mexico.
In the video above, you can watch Starship plunge through the clouds, flip vertically, and, with surprising grace, ease itself between the waiting arms of Mechazilla at around 4:20 PM ET.

title_en: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
title_fa: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
excerpt_en: The petition had attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon.
excerpt_fa: The petition had attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon.
content_en:
A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate the company’s recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang appears to have attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon.
The petition website said the signers include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders. Notable supporters include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan.
The petition states that its signers are “concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process” and demands that the board “bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts.” It also calls on the board to ensure a fair investigation and provide more information to the public.
“Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice,” the petition says.
Huang resigned on Thursday, four days after confessing to having an affair with a chip executive suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. The former CEO has agreed to testify before Congress, while news reports have also suggested that Huang engaged in multiple extramarital affairs.
Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as the company’s interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement. Nvidia’s stock price fell sharply through the week, while Huang’s departure is also expected to leave a big gap in AI industry funding.

title_en: The reasons why your TV soundbar has an audio delay
title_fa: The reasons why your TV soundbar has an audio delay
excerpt_en: Audio delays are really irritating, especially when watching sports and live events. We've got several possible causes and what you can do about them.
excerpt_fa: Audio delays are really irritating, especially when watching sports and live events. We've got several possible causes and what you can do about them.
content_en:
The reasons why your TV soundbar has an audio delay
And several possible fixes.
One of the more frustrating experiences you can have while watching TV comes when the audio is out of sync with the video. You've probably noticed it while viewing a show or a movie where the characters' mouth movements don't match the dialogue. Or when you're watching a sporting event and the play-by-play announcer calls a game-winning basket, touchdown or home run before you even see it.
Audio delay is a fairly common occurrence with soundbars connected to TVs, and there are a few reasons why this happens. Fortunately, audio delays can often be fixed pretty easily by simply adjusting some settings on your smart TV.
How the audio between your smart TV and soundbar gets delayed
Understanding the source of the audio delay between your smart TV and soundbar can help you determine how to fix it. For example, if you notice the audio delay while watching TV through your cable or a streaming service, try watching something from another source, like a Blu-ray player. If the audio from the Blu-ray syncs just fine, the issue could be with the actual cable broadcast or streaming service.
But if the audio delay occurs regardless of what you're watching, then the culprit is likely either your TV or soundbar, or a combination of both. First, check the connection between your TV and soundbar. If the digital optical cable or HDMI cable is loose, tighten it or connect a new one and try again. It may seem obvious, but a bad connection is often the issue.
The problem could also be the result of audio processing delays. Here's why. When you're only using your TV's speakers for audio, the TV is doing all the work behind the screen as it sends the video and audio only when the processing of both signals is complete. That results in completely synced audio and video. When you introduce a soundbar or other home theater system component to the process, an extra layer of processing happens. Your TV decodes the video, and your soundbar decodes the audio. If those decoding processes are off by even a fraction of a second, it's enough to delay the audio while the video has already been decoded and processed. That's when you get really annoying, out-of-sync dialogue and sound.
Of course, other factors can contribute to audio delay as well. The TV, the soundbar, a streaming device, a gaming console, and even poor Wi-Fi or Bluetooth wireless connections can also cause lag.
How to fix soundbar audio delay issues
Obviously, different brands of soundbars will have slightly different settings and controls. For Samsung soundbars, you can use the Sound Control button on the remote to adjust the audio until it aligns correctly. The remote also features an Audio Sync button, which allows you to use the Skip Forward/Backward buttons to adjust the sound until it's right. Also try the Audio Sync +/- feature for sync adjustments.
Similarly, LG soundbars have an AV Sync feature that can help you resync the audio to line up with the video. If you have a Sonos soundbar, you can go into the Sonos app on your phone and navigate to System > [select your soundbar] > Home Theater > TV Dialog Sync and adjust the slider until the audio syncs to the video.
There's also a handy way to completely bypass the TV, called direct routing. This is accomplished by plugging your cable box, streaming device or gaming console right into your soundbar's HDMI input. Then connect the other end of the HDMI cable to an HDMI output on your TV, and the audio decoding skips the TV and the processing delays it can cause by going directly into the soundbar.
Adjust your TV settings to solve audio delay problems
Oftentimes, a simple adjustment of your TV's settings can do the trick. One easy fix is to disable the extra audio and video modes and processing that the manufacturer of your TV advertises as high-end features. You've probably noticed these in your settings menu — features like digital noise reduction, dynamic contrast, game mode, movie/cinema mode, virtual surround sound, dialogue enhancers and 3D audio. Yes, these features can help with audio/visual quality, but they also require extra processing time, which leads to audio lag. Disabling or turning those features off can reduce the delay enough to ensure your soundbar's audio syncs with the TV's video.
HDMI ARC (Audio Return Channel) hardware in the TV and soundbar is also a common cause of audio delay because it doesn't have the bandwidth to pass high-end, uncompressed audio like Dolby TrueHD, DTS-HD Master Audio or 5.1 surround sound through the HDMI cable to the soundbar without taking extra time to turn those signals into lower-quality, passable audio. Upgrading to eARC solves this problem. If your TV and your soundbar both have HDMI eARC ports, all you need is an ultra-high-speed HDMI cable to connect them. If neither your TV nor your soundbar has an HDMI eARC port, direct routing is probably the best way to go.
You could also change your TV's audio format or source device to PCM or stereo to cut down on processing time. But that eliminates surround sound audio, which is probably one of the reasons you bought a soundbar in the first place. A better solution is to search your TV's settings for features like Lip Sync, AV Sync, Audio Delay or Audio Sync within the TV's audio or sound menu. Any of these allow you to adjust the audio delay setting until you get it just right. And if all else fails, try to reboot or reset all your home theater components by unplugging them for about a minute, then plug them back in one at a time and see if there's a difference. It's also a good idea to update your devices' firmware to ensure any bugs are being fixed.

title_en: Why some USB ports are yellow (and less common than others)
title_fa: Why some USB ports are yellow (and less common than others)
excerpt_en: Not every USB port color means what you think. Learn why yellow ports are so uncommon and what to check before you plug in anything important.
excerpt_fa: Not every USB port color means what you think. Learn why yellow ports are so uncommon and what to check before you plug in anything important.
content_en:
Why some USB ports are yellow (and less common than others)
Yellow USB-A ports usually mean Always On charging, but the particulars are up to the manufacturer.
A yellow USB port usually marks an "Always On" port, meaning it will continue to charge your device once you turn the computer off. It's one of several colors on USB-A ports, but none are an industry standard.
For example, the USB Implementers Forum (USB-IF) recommends one insert color, a specific blue, to help people tell the difference between USB 2.0 and USB 3.0 ports. However, this is just a suggestion, not a mandate. Every other color, yellow included, is a convention manufacturers can follow or not.
Lenovo, for example, jumps around with colors. The older IdeaPad Y400 and Y500 feature yellow USB-A ports that are specifically for Always On charging. Later Lenovo models dropped the yellow entirely and replaced it with battery icons.
Always On still needs power, and sometimes a setting
Yellow USB-A ports are not a common sight because they're a specialty feature that manufacturers only include on specific enterprise or business laptops. Manufacturers are also shifting toward symbols instead of a variety of colors.
A battery symbol next to a USB port indicates a port that's good for charging. A trident symbol also indicates the USB implementation, like USB 3.0 or USB4. On top of that, USB-C ports on many PCs and laptops are skipping the color coding entirely, since one connector shape tends to cover a wide range of capabilities.
If you come across a yellow port, don't assume it's ready to roll right out of the box. Depending on the PC or laptop, you may have to enable the Always On setting in the BIOS. Some laptops also ship with the "Charge in Battery Mode" disabled, so you can only charge devices when the laptop is plugged into AC power.
Which USB port color is faster?
Red is generally the fastest of the color-coded USB-A ports and is commonly used for 10 Gbps to 20 Gbps connections. Yellow doesn't really have a spot on the speed ladder, and color charts can't even agree on its place. Corsair lists yellow ports as either USB 2.0 or USB 3.0, and USB Memory Direct's color guide places yellow on a level playing field with red.

title_en: How to clear the cache on your Samsung TV
title_fa: How to clear the cache on your Samsung TV
excerpt_en: Your TV's cache is a collection of temporary files, some of which you don't need anymore. Here's why you might want to clear those out – and how.
excerpt_fa: Your TV's cache is a collection of temporary files, some of which you don't need anymore. Here's why you might want to clear those out – and how.
content_en:
How to clear the cache on your Samsung TV
If your apps or menus have been a bit sluggish, it's worth a try.
It's happened to many of us at some point. You've settled into the couch in front of your smart TV, and you just started binging your favorite show, watching that new release you've been waiting for weeks to see or anxiously anticipating the start of a big playoff game when ... your streaming app crashes.
Your first instinct may be to throw the remote across the room or immediately start browsing online for TV sales. Understandable reaction. But before you do any of that, take a deep breath and try one potential fix that could solve the problem if your TV is a Samsung: clearing the cache. Temporary cache files are stored every time you use an app, so they build up over time. The more apps you use, the more the cache grows. Eventually, that can impact your TV's performance.
Taking just a couple of minutes to clear the cache may take care of your TV's streaming issues. And don't worry, clearing your TV's cache will not delete any apps you've downloaded, mess with any of your audio/video settings, reset your Wi-Fi password or erase any software updates.
The benefits of clearing the cache on your TV
What clearing the cache on your Samsung TV will do is remove all temporary junk files that could be causing performance issues with the TV. So, if your streaming apps — like Hulu, Netflix, HBO Max, Peacock, Prime Video, YouTube and others — have been freezing or crashing when you're trying to watch them, clearing the cache may fix those issues.
Another common symptom you may encounter is extra lag or buffering as you browse through your Samsung TV menus or start up your apps; a glut of old cache data could be the culprit. Clearing it out should improve your TV's overall response time and result in smoother operation. Also worth noting is that most smart TVs have limited internal storage — typically around 8GB. However, the actual amount of available storage is far less.
For example, your Samsung TV's operating system gobbles up around 20 percent of the TV's total storage. When you factor in all the pre-installed bloatware, the apps you actually want to install and then the cache and temporary data files, there's not much storage left to spare. Clearing out all the built-up cache can free up some space to keep your apps running smoothly. Keep in mind, however, that the cache will pile up again as you continue to run apps. It's a good idea to make cache clearing a regular task every few months.
The downsides of clearing your TV's cache
There really aren't any lasting downsides to clearing your Samsung TV's cache. You're just getting rid of temporary junk files, after all. But you may experience a few minor inconveniences that are easily taken care of.
One annoyance is slower initial app loads, which occur because the app must download new temporary files (remember, you just deleted all the old ones) and images from online sources instead of loading them from the files that were locally stored on your TV. It's just a few extra seconds to wait for the first launch of each app after you cleared the cache, and subsequent launches shouldn't experience any delays.
Another small inconvenience, if you opt to Clear Data instead of Clear Cache, is the possible loss of saved app preferences, such as video playback, app layout or subtitle/closed captioning within certain apps. And you may notice within each app that some visuals like movie posters, thumbnails and other images take an extra beat to load. This happens for the same reason that the app takes an extra few seconds to launch after the TV's cache has been cleared.
How to clear your Samsung TV's cache
Clearing the cache on your Samsung smart TV is pretty quick and straightforward. And these instructions should apply to most Samsung TV models. We'll provide directions for Samsung TVs dating back to 2016 because they do vary slightly.
To clear the entire system cache for Samsung TV models made between 2020 and today, go to Settings > Support > Device Care > Start Device Care. If you want to clear the cache of individual apps, follow the same path, but choose Manage Storage rather than Start Device Care, select the app, click View Details > Clear Cache.
For 2019 and 7-Series Samsung TV models, follow Settings > Support > Self Diagnosis > TV Device Manager > Clean Now (to clear your TV's entire system), or choose an app and clear its cache from there. If you have a Samsung TV made between 2016 and 2018, you won't be able to clear caches of individual apps. But you can delete browser cookies as well as some internet data by going to Settings > Broadcasting > Expert Settings > HbbTV Settings > Delete Browsing Data.
Clearing the cache of your TV or individual apps should help with performance. If all else fails, you can always give your TV a cold boot, which works on every Samsung smart TV regardless of when it was built. With the TV on, press and hold the power button on your Samsung TV remote until the TV shuts off and turns back on. That process lasts roughly five seconds. Or, unplug the TV's power cable from the wall (or power strip), then wait 30 to 60 seconds before plugging it back in. These physical resets completely shut down the TV's operating system and clear out temporary cache files.

title_en: SpaceX successfully catches Starship after launch for the first time
title_fa: SpaceX successfully catches Starship after launch for the first time
excerpt_en: While the company has pulled off this trick a few times with Super Heavy boosters, it was a first for the Ship.
excerpt_fa: While the company has pulled off this trick a few times with Super Heavy boosters, it was a first for the Ship.
content_en:
SpaceX successfully catches Starship after launch for the first time
While the company has pulled off this trick a few times with Super Heavy boosters, it was a first for the Ship.
SpaceX nailed its first catch attempt of the Starship upper stage, safely catching the Ship with the arms of the launch tower it left from in South Texas.
SpaceX launched Starship on Friday for its 15th test flight, in which it set out to achieve some of its most ambitious goals yet. The company had planned to demonstrate its first double catch, which would see the Super Heavy V3 booster return to the launch site to be caught by the tower's chopstick arms before the upper stage, or the part known as the Ship, attempted the same landing maneuver a day later. SpaceX has caught and reflown V1 Super Heavy boosters a couple of times so far, but it hasn't yet tried to catch the Ship until now.
While Flight 15 succeeded in carrying out some of its main objectives — including deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites to orbit and catching the Ship — the first stage booster experienced a problem on its way back down to Earth and aborted its catch attempt, instead changing course to splash down in the Gulf, where it exploded before hitting the water. The Ship, though, continued on its journey in orbit for roughly 22 hours following launch before heading back down to the surface.
Mechazilla catches Starship! Congratulations to the entire SpaceX team on this incredible achievement! pic.twitter.com/YJzmGUZb2B
— SpaceX (@SpaceX) November 14, 2026

title_en: How to clear the cache on your Xbox Series X
title_fa: How to clear the cache on your Xbox Series X
excerpt_en: Clearing the cache on your Xbox Series X can help it retain its snappiness while avoiding glitches, or you can perform a console reset if all else fails.
excerpt_fa: Clearing the cache on your Xbox Series X can help it retain its snappiness while avoiding glitches, or you can perform a console reset if all else fails.
content_en:
How to clear the cache on your Xbox Series X
Keep your Xbox Series X feeling like new by keeping your cache clear, and if that doesn't help, a reset is in order.
If you secured your Xbox Series X years before the RAM crisis made consumer tech prices skyrocket (in case you were wondering why RAM prices are so high right now), chances are it's not as lag-free as it once was. Over time, temporary files can build up in the system, leading to slowdowns and glitches. When the classic restart option doesn't suffice, consider clearing the console's cache.
Just like clearing the cache on a phone or web browser, doing so on your Xbox once in a while can help its performance while navigating between menus. Clear the cache by turning off and unplugging your Xbox Series X for two minutes, then pressing the power button multiple times before reconnecting its power cord to power-cycle the console. Power it back on, and you should be good to go.
Clearing your cache is a trick worth trying when you run into excessive loading errors or connectivity issues in your games. For instance, Epic Games notes directly on its support site that clearing the cache on an Xbox Series X can help with load failure errors in its game Rocket League.
What to expect after clearing your Xbox Series X's cache
Clearing your cache can help resolve issues if a simple restart doesn't, since this action removes files stored on the console that may have been corrupted. Other ways to help reach the expected lifespan of your Xbox Series X are to routinely clean its vents for efficient heat management and keep the console in an open area so the fan can do its job.
The console's cache is supposed to store data over time to make common routines faster by reducing the need to repeatedly load the same elements. So while it's a design choice that's supposed to help, files can still build up over months and years, clogging things up. Rest assured that clearing your cache won't affect your games or save data.
One sign that you cleared your cache correctly is when you spot the Xbox logo on the screen and the full boot process occurs. However, a Reddit user wrote that clearing the cache could temporarily increase loading times in Microsoft Flight Simulator. Then again, a user also reported quicker boot times after clearing the cache, so your experience may vary.
Consider resetting your console if issues persist
While it's a good practice to clear your console's cache once in a while, there's no specific schedule you need to maintain. Simply doing so whenever your Xbox Series X feels sluggish should do the trick.
If your current experience is abysmal, you may even want to perform a reset. Before resetting, connect your console to the internet and let your save data sync to the Xbox network. To reset the console, go to Settings > System > Console info > Reset console. You can also select the option Reset and keep my games & apps to save yourself the hassle of redownloading everything, though you'll still need to sign back into your accounts afterward.
If your console still doesn't feel as snappy as you'd like or if your games don't run as expected after wiping its cache, consider a factory reset by choosing the option Reset and remove everything in the settings. While starting fresh with a factory reset can feel like a chore since it wipes everything on the console with all unsynced data lost (considering the wait time to redownload everything, along with the other drawbacks you should know before buying an Xbox Series X), it could get your games to run smoothly so you can once again enjoy your Xbox couch sessions.

title_en: Is your car tracking your location? Here's how to check and opt out
title_fa: Is your car tracking your location? Here's how to check and opt out
excerpt_en: Modern cars are great for farming user data, and big tech companies know it. It's important to know how this information is collected and how to opt out.
excerpt_fa: Modern cars are great for farming user data, and big tech companies know it. It's important to know how this information is collected and how to opt out.
content_en:
Is your car tracking your location? Here's how to check and opt out
Where you drive is your business. Your car may disagree.
If you drive a car built sometime in the past few years, it's almost certainly tracking your location. Modern vehicles function less like cars and more like computers on wheels these days, collecting data through GPS navigation, connected services, telematics systems and manufacturer apps.
While it all started innocently enough, with manufacturers using the collected data to understand how the cars were being driven, reasons behind crashes and so on and so forth, that data has become a source of income for them. The data can be shared with insurers, marketing companies and data brokers, sometimes without explicit driver consent.
As you'd expect, it all depends on what car make, model and year you are driving. Each will collect certain information based on what sensors are available, and you'll have to dig through the menus to even be able to cancel anything. Another way to ensure your car has less info on you is to avoid pairing your phone to it, as that gives it access to your contacts, call logs, music, location and more.
That means all those useful Android Auto and CarPlay features won't be available. But at least your car will spy less on you.
How do cars collect and share location data?
GPS navigation systems are the most obvious source due to how accessible apps such as Google Maps are thanks to Android Auto, but they're far from the only one. Connected service, telematics modules and those manufacture-branded apps they shove at you when you buy a car are continuously collecting information as you drive. These often log routes, destinations and driving behaviors in the background. When you think about data privacy, you don't really think about cars as being a potential problem.
And yet, the Mozilla Foundation has ranked cars as the worst product category it has reviewed for privacy. The reason? Just how extensively major automakers collect data on where you go and how you go there. Did you brake too hard? Did you almost get in an accident? Well, all that info might end up on the desk of your insurance company, affecting how much you pay each year. This isn't just some hypothetical concern as we already know that in January 2026 the FTC banned General Motors from sharing driver location data with consumer reporting agencies after the company violated its privacy commitments.
If you're wondering just how much information your car collects on you, there are ways to find out without tearing your car apart. Services like Privacy4Cars provide a free Vehicle Privacy Report that requires you to input your car's 17-character Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) (which you can find on the dashboard or door jamb). The report will tell you what your automaker and its service providers collect, share and sell. You can also check your automaker's privacy policy or connected-services terms, plus your car's manual to figure out what data is being collected.
How to tell if your car is being tracked by GPS and how to turn it off
Even if you don't generate such a report on your car, you can dig through your car's own settings. Most manufacturers' apps and dashboard menus include a privacy or data-sharing section where you can review what's being collected. It's worth checking both the app and the infotainment system directly, since settings aren't always mirrored across both. Look for keywords like Data sharing, Connected services, Analytics, Diagnostics, Location Services, Personalization, Voice assistant, Insurance sharing, Driver monitoring, and so on. Names can vary, based on manufacturer, car make and model, and so on, but you get the gist.
Opt-out options will also differ by manufacturers. Some will allow users to opt out of data sharing through dashboard settings, while others will offer more granular control rather than an all-or-nothing switch. You do have to keep in mind that disabling tracking usually comes with trade-offs as you might end up losing roadside assistance, that beloved remote start function that lets you heat up the car before you get on in the winter, smartphone integration or other features tied to location services. Before switching everything off, you should consider what exactly you're actually willing to give up on.
One thing to keep in mind, however, is that if you're selling or trading your vehicle, you should look into erasing your data, because it won't do so automatically. You'll need to perform a factory reset on the infotainment system, remove your account and vehicle from the manufacturer's app and even notify the manufacturer of the ownership change. Skipping this step means a stranger's driving habits might impact your own insurance profile and vice versa.

title_en: This built-in Windows tool can diagnose your PC's battery health
title_fa: This built-in Windows tool can diagnose your PC's battery health
excerpt_en: If your laptop doesn't seem to hold a charge as well as it used to, start by checking the diagnostics this tool can report. We'll show you how to use it.
excerpt_fa: If your laptop doesn't seem to hold a charge as well as it used to, start by checking the diagnostics this tool can report. We'll show you how to use it.
content_en:
This built-in Windows tool can diagnose your PC's battery health
It's a bit hidden, but it's easy to find if you know where to look.
The health and performance of a laptop's internal components are things that are important to keep a close eye on over its lifespan. A laptop's longevity is permanently linked to the status of its battery.
If you have a laptop, the battery is one that you may want to pay particularly close attention to. A failing or struggling battery will have some significant negative impacts on your laptop's performance, in addition to eventually being the thing that stops it from booting altogether.
Thankfully, there's a nifty, little-known Windows tool that can help you diagnose your laptop battery and its condition, as well as help you to determine when it may be time for you to look at a potential replacement. Perhaps more than any other type of computer out there, laptops are exceptionally difficult to diagnose sometimes, but this built-in tool can help make your life a little bit easier.
What is Powercfg and what does it do?
In addition to its many other built-in diagnostic tools, Windows offers one that is going to be quite handy if you happen to have a laptop. It's called Powercfg, and it's one of the most powerful utilities that you can use to help figure out what's going on with your laptop's battery.
To put it simply, Powercfg will allow you to monitor and maintain the energy and systems of your computer. If you're running it on a desktop computer, it will be beneficial in allowing you to monitor the energy efficiency of your PC, as well as alter certain sleep and hibernation states.
With a laptop, however, Powercfg becomes a much more powerful and comprehensive administration utility. Though it has its uses on PC, you'll be able to feel the impact of what it can do much more clearly when you run it on a laptop.
How to run Powercfg and keep tabs on your laptop's battery
If you've been noticing your laptop acting a bit strange lately, then Powercfg may be where you want to look first. The warning signs of a dying laptop battery range from something as subtle as slower charging than normal to the more severe — like a complete, random shutdown out of nowhere. You may also notice that the laptop itself starts to bulge, indicating a swollen battery with parts that are slowly breaking down.
Running Powercfg is fairly easy even for someone who isn't a computer expert. You only need to know how to type and how to open the Terminal window as an administrator. Begin by pressing Win+X, then clicking Terminal (Admin). The window that opens is where you'll type commands to engage with Powercfg. You can also use Command Prompt, which you invoke by pressing Win+R, typing cmd in the window that appears and pressing Enter.
To start with, one of the most helpful commands to use is powercfg /batteryreport. Type that exact line into Terminal and press Enter. This will give you a complete rundown of your laptop's current status as an HTML report that will save to your computer's files. The Terminal will tell you where to locate the file. You ideally want full charge capacity to be as close to design capacity as possible, which is what the laptop was built for. A bit of wiggle room is fine, but it's worth keeping an eye on if you think your battery isn't doing so great. Anything below 40 percent needs to be replaced, according to Dell.
Powercfg /energy will run a check on your battery and the laptop's efficiency. It lasts 60 seconds and also saves as an HTML report that you can open from the location indicated. This particular command will tell you which apps and devices may need to be reconfigured due to power drain on the battery. These two commands really go a long way in allowing you to self-diagnose battery trouble, and if you discover that the battery is severely damaged or causing issues with the laptop, it's most likely time to replace it with a new one.

title_en: Tesla opens Cybercab pre-orders ‘for personal use,’ with geo restrictions and a $299 monthly fee
title_fa: Tesla opens Cybercab pre-orders ‘for personal use,’ with geo restrictions and a $299 monthly fee
excerpt_en: Even Elon Musk said the monthly fee is "too high."
excerpt_fa: Even Elon Musk said the monthly fee is "too high."
content_en:
Tesla said on Friday evening that “select customers” now have the opportunity to pre-order the company’s autonomous, golden Cybercab “for personal use.”
More details became clear as those select customers looked at the order page. Tech reviewer Marques Brownlee posted that buyers “must accept delivery” in one of a handful of Texas cities and that the Cybercab will only operate in certain geofenced areas. The estimated delivery date is December 2026.
In addition to the $29,990 price tag, Cybercab owners will need to pay $299 per month to operate their vehicle.
In response to Brownlee’s post, Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the Cybercab “will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval.” He added that the monthly fee is “too high”: “Should match the cost of Tesla [Full Self-Driving] and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month.”
Tesla’s Ashok Elluswamy offered more information about the geofencing, saying that Cybercab will work “unsupervised inside all the same geo locations as @robotaxi, just serving the owners’ needs.”
After falling far short of projected sales, Tesla recently announced it will cease Cybertruck production next year and use the additional factory capacity to build more Cybercabs.

title_en: Change these Fitbit Edge settings for a better experience
title_fa: Change these Fitbit Edge settings for a better experience
excerpt_en: The Fitbit Edge not only looks good, but packs plenty of features while remaining minimal. To get the most out of it, you only need to tweak a few settings.
excerpt_fa: The Fitbit Edge not only looks good, but packs plenty of features while remaining minimal. To get the most out of it, you only need to tweak a few settings.
content_en:
Change these Fitbit Edge settings for a better experience
How to get more out of your fitness tracker.
For a while, the Fitbit brand seemingly had its back against the wall. After Google's takeover in 2019, it released a range of branded devices, like the Sense 2 and Charge 6, but the company really started to prioritize the Pixel Watch, to the point that people began questioning whether the brand would survive.
Recently, though, Google has reaffirmed its commitment to the Fitbit name with two new devices, led by the Fitbit Edge. It's arguably one of the best fitness trackers for people who don't want to spring for a full-fledged smartwatch. It might not be on par with something like the Garmin Forerunner 570 or Apple Watch Ultra 4, but it's not trying to be.
As with any tracker, there are a variety of settings on the Edge you can change to optimize your experience, from customizing its clock through to making it a bit more deadlift-friendly. None of these tweaks are strictly necessary, but you'll probably be glad to have them ready should the need arise.
The settings that immediately improve your Edge
One of the first things you should change is your Edge's watch face, or as Google refers to it, clock face. It's not just about style — some faces support more tiles (complications or widgets) than others, letting you check stats like calorie burn and heart rate at a glance, not just the time or weather. The best ones in that regard are the Modular faces, which allow up to four or five tiles.
To browse and install faces, open Google Health, then navigate to Connections > [your device] > Watch faces > Clocks. Pick what you want, then tap Install. On your Edge, you can swap installed faces at will by tapping and holding the screen.
One tweak that's surprisingly important is Tracker Orientation, again found under device settings in the Health app. This determines whether the physical button is on the left or right relative to onscreen content. You may need to flip orientation if you find that you're accidentally hitting the button during certain activities. When deadlifting, for example, I find that the straps I wear can easily bump up against a tracker's buttons unless I wear the device higher up on my arm.
If you're syncing data with a third-party service or just want fewer distractions, it may be worth disabling Coach Insights in Google Health. In the app, go to [Profile icon] > Google Health Settings > Coaching and select No Coach Insights. That way, you won't get unprompted summaries and advice popping up on your phone during the day. These might be completely pointless if you're a fitness veteran — someone who can run a 10K or squat 400 pounds probably doesn't need to be told what their data means.
Ways to stretch out battery life on the Edge
Under device settings in Google Health, you can configure GPS settings to always use your phone for location data instead of relying on the Edge's built-in GPS. This may significantly stretch out battery life, but be warned — you won't get any location data at all if you leave your phone behind. That could be a major problem with activities where carrying your phone is impractical, like swimming. If that's a concern, it's best to leave GPS settings on Dynamic, which will flip over to built-in GPS whenever your phone is missing.
If battery life is a high priority, be sure to also leave Always-On Display off. As convenient as it is, Google notes that the feature shrinks maximum battery life from seven days to around two. Real-world performance could be less, especially if onboard GPS is running. You should definitely switch the always-on display off if you're about to run a marathon or tend to forget about charging.
Lastly, consider charging your Edge a little bit every day. When your battery is running on fumes, even five minutes of charging may be enough to restore a full day's use. For those speeds, you do need to combine your cable with a 30W power adapter, but tossing your Edge on the charger while you shower is a great way to reduce battery anxiety.

excerpt_en: "It's really happening. I promise. For real." Those are the first words from Roy Graham, Head of Story at Magic: The Gathering, in a video posted yesterday announcing Planeswalker, the animated series heading to Netflix in 2027. An animated Magic: The Gathering series was first...

content_en:
“It’s really happening. I promise. For real.” Those are the first words from Roy Graham, Head of Story at Magic: The Gathering, in a video posted yesterday announcing Planeswalker, the animated series heading to Netflix in 2027.
Magic: The Gathering is getting a Netflix animated series. For real this time.
Magic The Gathering: Planeswalker is set to debut on Netflix in 2027.
Magic The Gathering: Planeswalker is set to debut on Netflix in 2027.
An animated Magic: The Gathering series was first teased back in 2019 with Joe and Anthony Russo at the helm. But that fell apart. In 2024, Netflix announced it still planned to make a series based on the game, but it decided to rework it from the ground up.
Now fans are finally getting their first glimpse of the show, which will be called Planeswalker. According to the sneak peek, because each plane exists in its own pocket universe, it will have a unique design, animation, and filmmaking style.
According to a synopsis of the show shared with IGN, Planeswalker will focus on Chandra Nalaar, a “volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past.” Storyline details beyond that are vague, other than mentioning an “insidious force” that Chandra and other Planeswalkers will team up to confront “to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence.”
